name: Pandava Thoothar Perumal Temple (Thiruppadagam), Kanchipuram
deity: Krishna as Pandava Thoothar Perumal, the envoy of the Pandavas, seated, with the Goddess Rukmini
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thiruppadagam in Kanchipuram, Krishna sits as Pandava Thoothar, the envoy of the Pandavas, in one of the largest seated images of Vishnu — a Divya Desam sung by the Alvars.

sections.history: Thiruppadagam is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Thondai Nadu. The temple is believed to have been built by the Pallavas in the late eighth century, with later contributions from the Medieval Cholas and the Vijayanagara kings. Three inscriptions on its walls survive: two of Kulothunga Chola I, who ruled from 1070 to 1120, and one of Rajadhiraja Chola, who ruled from 1018 to 1054. A stand-alone temple in its own right, unlike the four Divya Desams within the Ulagalantha complex, it stands in the western part of Kanchipuram.
sections.architecture: The temple faces east, and the sanctum is crowned by the Bhadra Vimanam. Its great image is the seated Krishna, some twenty-five feet tall by common account, among the largest seated images of Vishnu in the south, with the Goddess Rukmini. The sacred tank is the Matsya Theertham. In the front hall are kept the bronze festival images and the figures of the Alvars, and the carved stone work shows the hand of the Pallava and later builders.
sections.legends: The sthala purana recalls the Mahabharata. Krishna went to Hastinapura as the envoy of the Pandavas, seeking peace. Duryodhana, in his pride, had a pit dug and covered with a carpet and a gem-studded seat, hoping to trap the Lord. Krishna took his cosmic form, the Vishwarupa. Janamejaya, a descendant of the Pandavas, hearing this story from the sage Vaisampayana, is said to have performed penance here to see that form; the image of Pandava Thoothar answers that wish.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the great Vaishnava observances: Vaikunta Ekadashi, the annual Brahmotsavam with processions of the festival images through the streets of Kanchipuram, and the recitation of the Divya Prabandham in the month of Margazhi. Krishna's birthday, Gokulashtami, is also honoured with special worship here. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Few Divya Desams offer a sight as imposing as the seated Pandava Thoothar, whose scale draws the eye the moment the sanctum opens. Spend time in the front hall with the Alvars and the bronze images, and ask the priests to tell the story of the carpeted pit and the Vishwarupa. Combine the visit with Ulagalantha Perumal and the other Vaishnava temples of Kanchipuram.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi and festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple stands in Kanchipuram, in the western part of the old town, reached by road from Chennai, about 70 km to the north-east. Kanchipuram town is the nearest railhead and Chennai the nearest major airport; auto-rickshaws and local buses connect the temples of the town.
